# Restore the Playwright 1.64 dependency update checks

## Context

PR #19690 updates Playwright 1.63 → 1.64 and cssnano 9.3.2 → 9.6.0. Its [current triage](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19690#issuecomment-6194075653) leaves the update blocked on the disabled-feature guard and three grid component witnesses. This ticket supplies one maintainer-owned repair on that existing PR.

Design authority: the installed Playwright feature list and the existing component contracts: ordinary drag must scroll without selecting text, native drag must retire the monitor, and adjacent grid regions draw one divider. Preserve these behaviours and assertions.

## The Problem

The copied disabled-feature list lacks Playwright 1.64's `AimEnabled` and `NetworkTimeServiceQuerying`; `glState.spec.mjs` intentionally rejects a stale copy. Separately, hosted `ClickFocus` and `DragScrollNativeDrag` report zero scrolling in their ordinary-drag controls, and `ColumnTrailingEdge` reports divider pixel differences. Version controls now isolate the failures to Chromium 156's grid sizing: body/Viewport stay bounded, but Grid containers with `min-height:auto` expand beyond their flex allocation. Mouse presses start outside the viewport and eight pixel samples read outside the PNG. Computed Grid overflow is `hidden/hidden` on Chromium 153 and `hidden/clip` on 156; setting only the Grid minimum height to zero restores the original geometry and all three assertions. Playwright 1.64 with Chromium 153 also passes. cssnano remains 9.3.2 in these controls, and the fixture uses development CSS, where the theme builder does not invoke cssnano.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/e2e/utils/gpuIntent.mjs` owns the single disabled-feature declaration. `test/playwright/unit/e2e/glState.spec.mjs` compares it with the installed Playwright bundle and verifies both launch profiles preserve it.
- `test/playwright/playwright.config.component.mjs` runs the affected component specs in one Chromium page at a time, serving this checkout through its own port and theme preflight.
- `test/playwright/component/apps/grid-focus/app.mjs` deliberately contains native drag-source rows alongside ordinary rows. The specs must prove which input path their pointer gesture enters.
- `resources/scss/src/grid/Container.scss` owns Grid's outer minimum size. Its scrollable View owns content overflow. Numeric Flexbox remains `N 1 0%`, preserving the existing layout contract.
- `ColumnTrailingEdge.spec.mjs` compares real boundary pixels with an inner divider; out-of-image `getImageData` produces transparent zero bytes, so bounds must be checked before interpreting RGB.

## The Fix

Keep both dependency updates on #19690. Add the two upstream feature names in their upstream order. Set `min-height: 0` on `.neo-grid-container`, letting a flex-sized Grid shrink below its content minimum while its View handles scrolling. Add viewport/screenshot bounds checks to the existing component witnesses, preserving every original gesture and scroll/selection/monitor/divider assertion. Retain the browser/version/CSS controls as the causal receipt.

Prescription checked: `gpuIntent.mjs` owns feature preservation; `grid/Container.scss` owns the measured minimum-size defect; the existing component specs own truthful gesture and pixel observations. The one-rule CSS control passed all three original assertions, so neither an input-dispatch change nor a global Flexbox rewrite is warranted.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behaviour | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Disabled features | Installed Playwright bundle | Both profiles preserve the upstream list | Guard fails on drift | Existing module JSDoc | `glState.spec.mjs` |
| Grid pointer witnesses | Existing drag/focus and trailing-edge contracts | Real input reaches its intended path; scroll/selection/monitor and single-divider assertions stay meaningful | Hold incompatible dependency | Existing spec JSDoc | Version-isolated event/geometry receipts and full affected files |

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The selected Playwright version passes the unchanged disabled-feature parity guard.
- [ ] AC-2: Version-isolated receipts identify the component failures' cause, including the actual pointer/native-drag path; no unsupported attribution to Playwright or cssnano.
- [ ] AC-3: All three full component files pass with the retained assertions, plus a discriminating control for any repair.
- [ ] AC-4: #19690 records the final dependency choice, exact-head validation and cross-family review; human merge remains separate.

## Out of Scope

Release-cut ownership, general test-runner redesign, unrelated flaky tests, shared runtime configuration, and changing drag UX without a demonstrated defect.

## Avoided Traps

No timeout increase or assertion relaxation to mask a wrong gesture. No synthetic-event-only substitute for real pointer input. No assumption that grouped dependency changes have one cause. No new parallel dependency PR.
